1.body: BODIVA (Bolsa de Dívida e Valores de Angola) is the regulated market where shares, Treasury bonds and corporate bonds are traded.
1.heading: The market

2.body: The Capital Markets Commission (CMC) regulates and supervises the market, listed companies and intermediaries.
2.heading: Who supervises it

3.body: You don''t buy directly on the exchange. Orders go through an intermediary registered with the CMC, such as a bank or a brokerage firm, where you open a securities account.
3.heading: How to take part

1.body: Buying a bond lends money to the State or a company. In return you receive interest, the coupons, and the face value at maturity.
1.heading: A loan

2.body: A bond''s price is quoted as a percentage of its face value. Below 100% you buy at a discount; above it, at a premium.
2.heading: Price and face value

3.body: Yield to maturity combines the coupons with the gap between the price paid and the amount repaid. On each bond''s page you can work it out for any price.
3.heading: Yield

1.body: To receive a dividend you must own the shares before the ex-dividend date. Anyone who buys on or after that date doesn''t get that payment.
1.heading: The ex-dividend date

2.body: Dividends and interest may be subject to Angola''s investment income tax (Imposto sobre a Aplicação de Capitais, IAC), usually withheld at source. The rate depends on the security.
2.heading: Taxes

3.body: Income, in your portfolio, shows the expected payments from what you hold.
3.heading: In your portfolio

1.body: A limit order sets the most you''ll pay or the least you''ll accept. It only executes at that price or better, and may not execute at all.
1.heading: Limit orders

2.body: Each trade has costs: the intermediary''s commission, exchange fees and often custody. On small amounts, costs weigh more on the result.
2.heading: Costs

3.body: Recording purchases, sales and fees in your portfolio shows each position''s actual result.
3.heading: Track it in your portfolio

1.body: The price shown is the last trade. The change compares it with the previous session''s close.
1.heading: Price and change

2.body: Volume is the number of securities traded, and trades are the number of transactions. With few trades, a single one can move the price a lot.
2.heading: Volume and trades

3.body: A thinly traded security can take time to find a buyer or seller. The Liquidity section on each page shows how often it trades.
3.heading: Liquidity

1.body: Shares and bonds can fall in value, and you may get back less than you invested.
1.heading: Prices move

2.body: With few holdings, results depend on a few companies. Spreading across issuers and security types reduces the weight of each one.
2.heading: Concentration

3.body: If you''ll need the money soon, you may have to sell at a bad time or without a buyer. Consider your time frame before investing.
3.heading: Time frame

1.body: A share is a fraction of a company''s capital. Shareholders share in the business''s results and risks.
1.heading: A piece of a company

2.body: The price comes from trades between buyers and sellers. It rises when demand outweighs supply at the current price and falls otherwise.
2.heading: How the price is set

3.body: Returns come from price changes and from any dividends the company decides to pay. Neither is guaranteed.
3.heading: Where returns come from

methodology.contributions: Contributions arrive at the end of each month and buy units at that month''s projected price. Stocks use whole units; funds allow fractional units. Uninvested cash stays available for the next contribution.
methodology.finalValue: The final value includes projected units and uninvested cash. We exclude dividends, taxes, fees and inflation. Bonds are unavailable because percentage quotes require additional data to calculate their monetary value.
methodology.quoteAndPrice: The quote retrieved from the server determines how many units you can buy. The annual price change you enter is an assumption, converted to an equivalent monthly rate and held constant throughout the period. It is not inferred from past performance.
methodology.title: How we calculate
